answers.stem_only: Network ACLs are stateless. The responses leave the instances to the client's ephemeral port, not to port 443, so the custom ACL drops them. Add an outbound ACL rule for TCP 1024-65535 to 0.0.0.0/0 (covers all client operating systems); do not open everything.
Add a gateway VPC endpoint for S3 to the private route tables. It has no hourly or data processing charge, keeps S3 traffic private and off the NAT gateway; keep the NAT gateway for internet updates.
The subnet is not public yet: its route table has only the local route. Add 0.0.0.0/0 to the internet gateway in the subnet's route table. The default network ACL already allows all traffic.

A VPC's primary CIDR cannot be changed or enlarged, and a secondary CIDR must not overlap existing ones. Add a non-overlapping secondary IPv4 CIDR block, create new subnets in it and add them to the Auto Scaling group.
Load balancer in public subnets in two AZs; application and database instances in private subnets (no internet gateway route, no public IPs) in the same two AZs. A subnet lives in one AZ only.
Reference the application tier's security group as the source of an inbound TCP 3306 rule in the database security group. It follows instances as they scale and is narrower than subnet CIDRs.

Replace NAT instances with managed NAT gateways (one per AZ for resilience): no patching, no failover scripts, bandwidth scales automatically. Update the private route tables to send 0.0.0.0/0 to them.

Security groups are stateful, so the REJECT of the response comes from the stateless network ACL of the service subnet, outbound direction. Add an outbound ACL rule on the service subnet for the Linux ephemeral range (32768-61000) to the client subnet CIDR only.

Use an egress-only internet gateway for IPv6 outbound-only access, with a ::/0 route to it in the private subnet's route table. It blocks inbound-initiated IPv6 connections regardless of security groups.

Every public IPv4 address (including Elastic IPs in use) is billed hourly. Move the instances to private subnets without public IPv4 addresses and send outbound traffic through NAT gateways; a few NAT gateways with small data volumes cost far less than 400 public IPv4 addresses.

Elastic IPs do nothing without a route to an internet gateway. Keep the subnet private: create a NAT gateway in the public subnet, route 0.0.0.0/0 from the private route table to it, and release the unneeded Elastic IPs.

Security groups have no deny rules; network ACLs do. Add a lower-numbered inbound deny rule for the malicious range to the network ACL of the public subnets (which hold both the load balancer and the instances). AWS WAF would also work if offered.
A subnet is in exactly one AZ. Create a subnet in a second AZ and run instances in both subnets behind the load balancer (for example with an Auto Scaling group across both).

Add an S3 gateway endpoint to the subnet's route table; its prefix-list route is more specific than 0.0.0.0/0, so S3 traffic uses the endpoint. Keep the 0.0.0.0/0 route to the internet gateway for the partner website.
Flow logs capture only metadata, not payloads. Use VPC Traffic Mirroring on the instances' network interfaces with the Network Load Balancer (UDP listener for VXLAN) as the mirror target.

S3 gateway endpoints cannot be reached from on premises over Direct Connect or VPN. Create an S3 interface endpoint (PrivateLink) in the VPC and have the on-premises servers use its endpoint-specific DNS name over the private VIF.
A NAT gateway is zonal. Add a NAT gateway in a public subnet in the second AZ and route each private subnet to the NAT gateway in its own AZ. No extra standby gateways needed.

Use a free S3 gateway endpoint on all private route tables to remove S3 traffic from the NAT gateway, and put a NAT gateway in each AZ with workers, routing each subnet to its own AZ, to remove cross-AZ data transfer for the internet downloads.

Use one regional NAT gateway in automatic mode: it expands to the AZs where the VPC has workloads and contracts when they leave, needs no public subnet per AZ, and every private subnet routes 0.0.0.0/0 to the one gateway ID.

Both compute and NAT must exist in a second AZ: create a private subnet in a second AZ and run workers in both subnets, and create a NAT gateway in a public subnet in that second AZ with each private subnet routed to the NAT gateway in its own AZ. Do not add gateways in AZs with no workers.

Set the source of the instances' inbound HTTPS rule to the load balancer's security group. Only the load balancer can then reach the instances; load balancer node IPs change, so do not use IP addresses.
Zonal resilience is not needed in this test environment, so the cheapest design is to keep the single NAT gateway and change nothing.
